Moqbal Ahmed, Advocate-For the Defendant ----- Petitioner. 
Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocate-For the Plaintiff ----- Opposite Party.
parties:
Ganesh Chandra Das ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Arati Acharjya ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
In this civil Revision a Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Arati Acharjya to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 15-2-1995 and 22-2-1995 respectively passed by Mr Hasan Shaheed Ferdous, learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong in Family Appeal No. 46 of 1994 affirming the judgment and decree passed by Mr Md Golam Sarwar, learned Assistant Judge, Additional Court No. 3 Chittagong in paribarik Money Suit No. 6 of 1993 allowing maintenance for the wife and 3 children, should not be set aside. 

 2. The Revisional application was filed mainly on the grounds that the judgments and decrees of both the Courts below are not on the basis of legal evidence on record and both the Courts below committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, that the trial court misread and misconstrued the evidence on record and the Court of appeal below did not assess the evidence on record independently and thereby committed error of law occasioning a total failure of justice; that the Family Court has been constituted under the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 only for the Muslim Community, hence the trial court below committed error of law by decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiff who is a member of the Hindu Community and, as such, the Family Court and the trial Court has no jurisdiction to deliver the impugned judgment and decree and the Court of appeal below also committed error of law causing failure of justice. 

 4. The trial Court discussed the evidence of both the sides but did not believe the alleged illicit connection of plaintiff-opposite party with Advocate Kamal and observed that Muslim Family Courts Ordinance of 1985 is a procedural law applicable to the citizens of all religions living in Bangladesh and the trial Court decreed the suit for maintenance of Taka 200 for the plaintiff and Taka 200 for each of the 3 children and directed the defendant petitioner to pay Taka 55,200 within 60 days and to pay Taka 800 as maintenance of the aforesaid 4 persons within 7 days of the following month. 

 5. Defendant petitioner preferred Family Appeal No. 46 of 1994 in the court of learned District Judge, Chittagong, The learned Subordinate Judge, Chittagong heard the appeal, discussed the evidence on record and the law points involved therein and delivered the impugned judgment dated 15-2-1995 and the decree dated 22-2-1995 affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court giving rise to the filing of this revisional application. 

 6. Mr Moqbul Ahmed, learned Advocate for the petitioner, argued supporting all the grounds mentioned in the revisional application, and submits that all the 3 children of the plaintiff opposite party have become adult and major by this time and they are serving in Garment Factories and the plaintiff opposite party is also serving in a Garments factory and they are not entitled to any maintenance from the side of defendant petitioner; referring to the evidence of DWs, particularly DW 2, the learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that there is corroborative evidence that the plaintiff opposite party was leading an immoral life with illicit connection with one Advocate Mr Kamal and she went to Cox's Bazar and different cinema halls with Mr Kamal and she was found in her bedroom with Mr Kamal and under the circumstances the plaintiff opposite party is not entitled to get any maintenance. The learned Counsel for the petitioner filed a supplementary affidavit dated 31-7-2001 sworn by one Sultan Ahmed, son of Amir Hamja, Patiya District, Chittagong and pointed out to the certified copy of 3 Birth Registers Annexure A series signed by Chief Health Officer of Chittagong City Corporation showing dates of birth and submits further, that all the 3 children are now adult and major and under the law they are not entitled to get any maintenance from their father defendant petitioner and that the learned court of appeal below committed error of law and miscarriage of justice by the impugned judgment and decree. 

 7. Mr Khorshid Alam Khan assisted by Mrs Farida Yesmin and Mr Syed Ziaul Hossain refuted all the grounds mentioned in the Revisional application and the points raised by the learned Advocate for the petitioner and submits that the learned trial Court decreed the suit for maintenance on the basis of legal evidence on record and that the learned Subordinate Judge as a court of appeal below discussed the evidence on record and the law points involved therein and upheld the judgment and decree of the trial Court and that the court of appeal below committed no error of law and no miscarriage of justice. The learned Counsel for the opposite party submitted a counter-affidavit dated 30-7-2001 sworn by Arati Acharjya, plaintiff opposite party and submits that due to physical and mental torture inflicted by defendant petitioner upon the plaintiff opposite party and for stopping maintenance of the plaintiff there was a salish and it was decided that the defendant petitioner would give maintenance of Taka 1800 per month for his wife and 3 children and that the plaintiff opposite party had no immoral connection with Advocate Kamaluddin who is also a rich man. 

 12. The trial Court examined the evidence on record and commented that the alleged illicit connection between plaintiff opposite party and Advocate Kamal was not proved by direct evidence; hence the trial Court decreed the suit and did not deprive the plaintiff opposite party from the maintenance. 

 16. On a careful scrutiny of the documentary and oral evidence on record it appears that there was a salish between the parties and the Salishnama Ext 4 was prepared with signature of both the sides and it was decided that defendant petitioner was to pay Taka 12,600 including maintenance for 7 months from December, 1987 upto June, 1988. The judgment and decree passed by the trial Court are based on legal evidence on record and the learned Subordinate Judge recorded concurrent findings and decisions after discussing the evidence on record and after recording proper reasonings. 1 find nothing to say that the court of appeal below committed error of law and any miscarriage of justice. According to the case-law reported in 50 DLR 166 Abdur Rahim vs Arifur Rahman, a court of Revision can interfere with the findings of facts by the court of appeal below as a final court of facts only in exceptional circumstances when the findings are shockingly perverse. 

 17. For the aforesaid reasons the impugned judgment and decree are not found to be perverse. From the birth registers supplied by the defendant petitioners it appears that Lilu Rani Das is now more than 24 years old, Liton Chandra Das is 22 years old and the youngest daughter Lipi Rani Das is now 20 years old. 

 18. In the light of my findings and discussions made above and in view of the provisions of section 2(d) Of the Children Marriage Restraint Act, 1929 Lilu Rani Das and Liton Chandra Das will get maintenance from their father defendant petitioner upto age of 18 years from December, 1987 and Lipi Rani Das, youngest daughter, will get maintenance till her marriage and plaintiff opposite party the wife will get the maintenance as per terms and conditions laid down by the trial Court in the judgment and decree. Only with this modification due to legal necessity the impugned judgments and decrees of both the courts below are hereby upheld.
